lens: Information and discoverability — long or difficult content (simulated AI review lens)
reason: The public proposition, audience-specific navigation, engagement terms and student preparation are clear in source. Supplied homepage captures show a coherent Precision Instrument hierarchy, with readable prose separated from compact labels and repeated next steps. I traced the client journey from services through fee/confidentiality FAQs to contact; the recorded desktop/mobile test confirms navigation and a synthetic inquiry receipt, not real delivery or observed user success. Canonical/social metadata, private noindex defaults and request-time case lookup are credible local foundations. However, recruitment failure can be described as a Board publication decision. Correct that factual state before release. World-class acceptance remains unproven without difficult-content and hosted evidence; client-approved case studies are absent rather than fabricated.
inspected: src/app/apply/application-form.tsx: MaterialsStep and ReviewStep privacy copy

findings.evidence: fetchPublicRecruitment discards the RPC error and maps absent data to {cycle:null}. Join defaults missing events to [] and then states “The Board has not published events for this cycle yet,” while replacing application access with recruitment updates.
findings.userImpact: During a returned RPC failure, students can mistake unavailable dates for an unpublished cycle and defer checking an actual recruitment deadline. The page asserts an editorial fact it has not established.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve a distinct unavailable result. Show temporary date-loading failure and a retry/contact or application-status route; reserve the unpublished-events statement for a successful empty response. Add a targeted failed-RPC journey assertion.

findings.evidence: Preparation tells students to ask current members about time commitment; the weekly-commitment FAQ repeats that request instead of giving an expected load. The surrounding long page supplies materials and evaluation detail but no workload estimate.
findings.userImpact: Students assessing a difficult semester cannot determine whether membership fits their schedule without a separate conversation, even after locating the relevant FAQ.
findings.suggestedFix: Obtain an owner-approved current-cycle workload range, recurring obligations and peak-week caveat, and publish them near preparation with an update date. Do not invent hours.

notVerified: No hosted deployment, Clerk/Supabase/storage/email integration, human study or observed user success exists in this evidence.
No Join/work capture or rendered maximum-length case study was supplied; narrow-screen long titles, 4000-character contexts and large method/deliverable lists remain unverified.

Publication proof uses a short synthetic HTTP fixture. It establishes page publication/withdrawal and generated PNG responses, not hosted approval/RLS, crawler indexing, social-platform cache removal or measured SEO gains.

Physical devices, Safari/Firefox, assistive technology and live authenticated applicant/operator journeys were not exercised by this seat. Original-resume disclosure was inspected; policy approval and retention remain external decisions.
